You may give any whole number of these stickers, from 0 through 10, to a pictured stranger of your own age and gender, keeping the rest. Giving k stickers leaves you with 10-k and gives the stranger k. Sharing is optional, and you are explicitly told that it provides no benefit to yourself and that no one will know how many stickers, if any, you share. After the instructions, you are left alone for 2–3 minutes to put the stickers you want to give into a separate bag. The recipient is absent and does not make a return, rejection or other choice. This sharing task comes last in the assessment battery, rather than necessarily immediately after a drumming task. Earlier task performance and its timing are not supplied; do not infer them. This is the year 2 follow-up task, with a single stranger recipient. No later assessment or other child's response is available here. Predict observed human sharing rather than recommend an allocation. Output only the integer number of stickers placed in the sharing bag, from 0 to 10, without an explanation.
